chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
That he was asked about a man who has only one garment, and salat (prayer) is not permissible in it, and he cannot find water to wash it—what should he do?
He said: «He performs tayammum and prays; then when he finds water, he washes it and repeats the salat (prayer).»

Because the intended meaning in this report is the state of necessity in which he is unable to remove the garment due to cold or something else; at that point he prays in it, and after that he repeats the salat (prayer).

key_terms.أَعَادَ الصَّلَاةَ: he repeats the salat (prayer) after the impediment is removed
key_terms.ثَوْبٌ وَاحِدٌ: a single garment, the only clothing available to the person
key_terms.حَالَ الضَّرُورَةِ: a state of necessity that affects the legal ruling
key_terms.لَا تَحِلُّ الصَّلَاةُ فِيهِ: salat (prayer) is not valid in it, due to impurity or legal unsuitability
key_terms.نَزْعِ الثَّوْبِ: removing the garment, which is not possible in the described circumstance
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, the dry ablution used when water is unavailable

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if their only garment is unsuitable for salat (prayer) and no water is available to wash it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person who possesses only one impure garment and cannot wash it due to lack of water. In a state of necessity, he performs tayammum and prays in it, then once water becomes available he washes the garment and repeats the salat (prayer).
